public_rationale: The public-record review supports the narrow disclosure claim. OpenAI's release materials contain no GPT-4 training-water figure, and contemporary independent assessments corroborate the reporting gap. No qualifying disclosure dated by February 10, 2024 was located. Microsoft-wide totals and outside estimates do not contradict a claim about what OpenAI disclosed.
limitations: A negative disclosure claim cannot exclude an obscure or subsequently removed publication with absolute certainty.
The independent assessments precede the post; searches for intervening disclosures found none.
This finding does not establish how much water GPT-4 actually consumed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has never disclosed the water consumption figures for GPT-4.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI has never disclosed those numbers for GPT-4; I can scarcely imagine what they will be for GPT-5.
statement.document_title: Seven reasons why the world should say No to Sam Altman

our_interpretation: Those numbers refers principally to GPT-4 training water consumption, following the comparison with estimated GPT-3 training water use.
Disclosed means made public by OpenAI. Third-party estimates or Microsoft-wide water totals do not constitute an OpenAI disclosure of GPT-4's consumption.
Never describes the public record through February 10, 2024, including any pre-release disclosures; no artificial starting date is imposed.
The remark about scarcely imagining GPT-5 figures supplies no separate testable forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Review of relevant OpenAI disclosures, corroborated by contemporary research on reporting gaps, finds no publicly disclosed GPT-4 training-water figure through the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An authenticated OpenAI disclosure published by February 10, 2024 gives a quantitative GPT-4 training-water figure.
